reference_sql:
SELECT promo_type, SUM(end_date - start_date + 1) AS promo_days
FROM promotions
GROUP BY promo_type
alternatives: SELECT promo_type, SUM(date_diff('day', start_date, end_date) + 1) AS promo_days FROM promotions GROUP BY promo_type

WITH runs AS (  -- one row per promotion
  SELECT promo_type, end_date - start_date + 1 AS days_running
  FROM promotions
)
SELECT promo_type, SUM(days_running) AS promo_days
FROM runs
GROUP BY promo_type
SELECT promo_type, SUM(end_date - start_date) + COUNT(*) AS promo_days FROM promotions GROUP BY promo_type

other_way.sql:
WITH runs AS (  -- one row per promotion
  SELECT promo_type, end_date - start_date + 1 AS days_running
  FROM promotions
)
SELECT promo_type, SUM(days_running) AS promo_days
FROM runs
GROUP BY promo_type
other_way.tradeoff: Working out each promotion's days in a step first makes the grain plain, but one SUM over the expression is shorter.

FROM promotions
